correctness.rationale: For a fixed label-2 support T, edges with neither endpoint touched by T must have label 1, and any other edge outside T can have label 0. An extraneous 1 can be lowered; therefore every global minimum is its unique canonical completion, with cost 2|T|+|U(T)|. Supports of size at least 6 have cost at least 12. Independently generated GP(8,3) edges and enumerated all 55,455 smaller supports by their endpoint sets. By sizes 0 through 5 the minimum costs were 24,21,18,15,12,11, with respective multiplicities 1,24,132,184,54,72. All 72 global optima have exactly five 2s, one 1, and eighteen 0s. Pairwise intersection size four on the optimal supports gives exactly 96 exchanges, none preserving the single edge. The 24 degree-four and 48 degree-two vertices form the two parts; the branch-neighbor pairs of the degree-two vertices are distinct. I suppressed them and found a complete adjacency-preserving bijection to the line graph by independent backtracking, not relying on the certificate's proposed bijection. I separately verified the certificate's states, exchanges, GP-to-LCF and branch-to-line-graph maps. Independent flood distances gave eccentricity 8 for all vertices, confirmed connectedness, and put the endpoints of the certified length-eight path exactly eight apart. Thus the claim is of an abstract subdivision, not of a natural indexing by the single edge.
residual_risks: Exact finite result for GP(8,3) under support replacement with canonical recompletion. It is not a result for all generalized Petersen graphs or ordinary coordinate swaps. The recorded output is supplementary to independent proof and enumeration.

claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: Neither a similar reconstruction on another state space nor the use of L(G) as the domination input entails that the optimal configuration graph itself is a subdivision of that input. The exact degree-two suppression and verified bijection are additional content.

evidence: Chang–Chen–Liu explicitly give gamma'_R(G)=gamma_R(L(G)); edges of G correspond to vertices of L(G) and the labeling condition carries over. Samodivkin's P1 fixes the label-1 set and P2 swaps a 2 and a 1, leaving the label-0 set fixed. No reviewed exchange fixes the label-1 edge, and an independent comparison of all 96 exchanges finds no P2 coincidence either: not one has both its incoming 2 equal to its previous 1 and its outgoing 2 equal to its new 1. P3 and P4 require one endpoint state to have two 1s, which these minima do not have.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: The vertex-Roman data for the line graph, if known, would count the same labelings. But a graph using the cited local swap rules is not an equivalent reconfiguration graph here; the support replacement plus recompletion allows transitions outside those rules.

value.rationale: A natural cubic symmetric benchmark supports more than a Roman domination number: the minimum labeling space recovers the original edge-incidence structure after suppressing forced degree-two states. The structure and metric data make it useful for comparing dynamics under different minimum-state exchange rules; here the support-recomputation rule even turns an edgeless local-swap graph on the same functions into a connected graph of diameter eight. The exact census alone would not imply these conclusions.
residual_risks: No general reconstruction theorem or geometry-only canonical bijection is claimed.
